newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it has evidence linking PLO to slayings.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it has evidence linking PLO to slayings.

text.p: Israeli police said on Sunday they had "solid evidence" that a security branch of the Palestinian Authority bore responsibility for the killing of two Palestinian land dealers.
"There is solid evidence that one of the Palestinian intelligence branches is responsible for the two cases in addition to the kidnapping," police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin told Reuters.

Menuhin said Israeli police on Saturday arrested six Palestinians as they were abducting an Arab land dealer in the Jerusalem area. She said four of the six worked for a branch of Palestinian security.
The man who was kidnapped was known to have cooperated with land dealer Ali Mohammad Jumhour, 34, found dead on Saturday, the spokeswoman said.

Jumhour was the third land dealer slain since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen said last month Arabs who sold land to Israel would face the death penalty. All three victims were shot in the head at close range.
Menuhin said the Palestinian intelligence branch, which she did not name, bore responsibility for the killing of Jumhour and Farid Bashiti, the first dealer killed.
Israeli officials had already said they suspected Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's administration was involved in the killings but PLO officials deny it.

"This is nonsense, the Authority is not involved in the killing of those dealers, brokers, traitors," Abu Medeen told reporters in self-ruled Gaza. "I accuse the Israelis, and I'm sure there is a finger of an Israeli in this assassination."
Earlier on Sunday, a Palestinian newspaper editor said a previously unknown Palestinian group had claimed responsibility for killing Jumhour on Saturday.

An anonymous caller, speaking Arabic, told the Palestinian daily al-Hayat al-Jadidah newspaper that the Keepers of the Holy Land Group shot Jumhour near Ramallah self-rule enclave in the West Bank on Saturday because of his dealings.

"The caller said his group, Keepers of the Holy Land, shot Jumhour dead because he sold land to Jews," Hafez al-Barghouthi, the newspaper's editor-in-chief, told Reuters. He said the caller had also contacted PLO police and other local newspapers.

Jumhour and another land dealer, 60 year-old Harbi Abu Sarah, were killed in Rafat near Ramallah, a village still under Israeli occupation. Bashiti was killed in al-Tireh village, also in the Ramallah area.

Abu Medeen said the Palestinian Authority had activated a Jordanian military law that once prohibited the sale of land to Jews. The new ban followed a crisis in PLO-Israeli peace moves over the start of construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

"It's a law. Those suspected of selling land will be questioned, interrogated, and then according to the law, the judge will decide maybe to confiscate their property, maybe to sentence them to life imprisonment or maybe the penalty will reach the death penalty," Abu Medeen said.

Last week, Abu Medeen said the PLO was interrogating up to 12 Palestinians suspected of selling land to Israelis. The PLO said the ban is needed to curb Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip and the West bank, including East Jerusalem, that could strengthen Israeli claims to sovereignty.
Washington and an international human rights group have urged Arafat to forbid retribution against land dealers.
